title: Chapter 3: The Former Protagonist and the Former Villain 2
content: Alicia and Mariana, these two women, were positioned as the villain and the protagonist in the game world.
A duchess and a commoner, they would never mix, but in the setting of the academy, they intertwined and caused a rejection reaction.
In the story, they were destined to fight until one of them was ruined, but reality was different.
"Alicia, you were a bento person too?"
"Since Lagna is, it's easier to make it together, right?"
"That mixed sandwich looks delicious."
"Do you want one?"
"Is it okay? I'll take it. In return, let me offer you my snack, scones."
The two of them were now happily eating their lunch on a bench behind the library.
How did it come to this?
It was all because of the fake protagonist, Patricia, who was currently enjoying a reverse harem paradise in the center of the vast courtyard.
How did she even get into the protagonist position?
Thanks to her, the plan to smoothly walk down the path of love, deal with the disasters that would arise, and live leisurely in the peaceful Brave Territory was falling apart.

Due to these unforeseen circumstances, the two of them were cast out from both the villain route and the protagonist route, yet by some twist of fate, they had become friends… that was the current situation.
"Where's Lagna? Didn't you always eat together?"
"I don't eat, you know? Don't you know even though we're in the same classroom?"
"Well? He always disappears during break time."
"…Are you attending class properly? Are you doing anything strange?"
"Yes, I stay in the classroom and attend seriously."
"Ugh, then where are you and what are you doing…?"
What am I doing, you ask?
I'm smiling down at this scene from the roof of the library.
If I were with her, the insults directed at her would increase since I'm a noble from the discarded land.

Watching my fiancée get insulted right in front of me would tarnish the Brave Family's name, but I figured that if I went to defend her head-on, Alicia would probably stop me, so I decided to act alone.
Still, who would have thought that the former villain and the former protagonist would meet like this?
Their encounter seemed like a desperate attempt by a distorted fate to return to its original course.
With the two of them together, something was bound to happen, and the circumstances surrounding them were becoming increasingly suspicious.
"Hmph, a cunning damaged girl hiding away. How stubborn to stay at the academy while hanging out with that stinky commoner. I wonder if she'll get expelled along with that commoner?"
"I think so too, Lady Ekaterina!"
"Right? This is an academy for nobles. That detestable girl named Patricia, I should personally kick her out! Ho-ho-ho!"
"Impressive as always, Lady Ekaterina!"
Here they come again, the group of harassing nobles.
Nothing particularly happened when Alicia was quietly spending time alone, but as soon as she started interacting with Mariana, they began sniffing around to harass her.
"How pathetic."
What are they so unhappy about? Can't they just leave her alone?
No one in my and Mariana's classroom would have such thoughts.
Having been too aware of their place, they had settled into the role of the class's small animals.
"That damaged girl will never find happiness! Let's go!"
With a few followers in tow, Ekaterina started to move, and I deployed a small barrier at her feet.
"Ugh!?"
"Lady Ekaterina!? Are you okay!? Oh no, a nosebleed!"
"Ouch… I tripped on something, and—brr, it's cold!?"
I smashed the barrier into one of the water pipes used to water the flowerbed in the back garden, splashing water right where Ekaterina had fallen.
"Uh, Lady Ekaterina… are you okay…?"
"Can't you see!? Of course, I'm not okay!!"
"Ouch."
"This is so disappointing! Hmph!"
Soaked to the skin, Ekaterina slapped the cheek of a worried follower and stormed back the way she came in anger.
"Too small-time for a new villain."
Ekaterina was originally one of Alicia's followers, who had upgraded from mob to villain after Alicia faded out.
Even though Alicia and Mariana should have exited the stage, it felt like something was working to return them to their original fate.
I was fulfilling the role of quietly brushing away the sparks from behind the scenes, using the fact that I originally didn't exist in the story.
"Impressive."
A voice came from behind me, and when I turned around, I saw the academy head, Volzeia, standing there.
"Isn't it wrong to harass others?"
"Your act of destroying equipment is also wrong."
The roof of the library is quite high, but he managed to climb up here.
Right now, it felt like we were both extending our hands to the actors behind the scenes.
"Are you weighing the safety of the students against the equipment, Headmaster?"
"I will charge the repair costs to the Brave Family."
"Please bill the Gran Oldwood Duke House. It's a poor territory in a remote area."
"Isn't Alicia under the Brave Family's care?"
"Yes, I will be more careful from now on."
Grrr, I can't argue with that.
I should reduce the intentional destruction of equipment.
"But if I were there, it would definitely complicate things, right?"
"That would seem to be the case."
"That would seem to be the case? What does that mean?"
"If you were in front of me, what could you do?"
This isn't my battlefield; this is Alicia's battlefield, and I'm fine being backstage.
What would I do in a place like that, covered in blood?
I commented that I was too aware of my place, but in reality, I was just like that.
"Then I'll be fine as a backstage worker."
Since I originally don't exist, that's just fine.
If I don't separate things from the start, it will become irretrievable once they mix.
"You are a student of the academy. You have the right to enjoy your youth."
"Yeah, I'm already enjoying my youth enough."
"Then did you give up and enroll from the start?"
Volzeia's words pierced through me, and I instinctively felt a surge of killing intent.
Did I give up and enroll? Absolutely not.
I didn't give up on this second crappy life.
In the long run, it's just three years.
If I can spend those three years peacefully, that's all I need.
"Besides, the person you want to protect isn't that weak right now."
"Could you please stop reading my mind?"
"I'm not reading your mind. But what will you do if you block the flow?"
The atmosphere was too serious.
The serious vibe emanating from the old man in front of me made me uncomfortable; I felt like I wanted to inject some Sebas energy into the situation.
"If the flow you blocked eventually bursts, the one swallowed by that muddy current will be the one you tried to protect."
"If you have something to say, just say it clearly. That's the Brave way."
Are you saying that the saintess won't awaken if this continues?
The serious atmosphere suggested that this old man knew something.
"Have you forgotten the pride of the Brave Family since coming to the Royal Capital—"
"—You'd better not provoke me carelessly."
I stopped my fist right in front of Volzeia.
A thud echoed as a shockwave passed behind the old man.
"I'm only doing this because it's the situation I desire. If anything happens to Alicia, I won't hold back. It doesn't matter if this is your little garden."
"If you desire that, then show me."
Not blinking even once, the sage's name isn't just for show.
I made a bold statement, but there was no reason to mess up the academy right now, so I decided to retract my fist.
"That's too abstract; I can't understand. If you have something to say, please say it clearly. I'm not good at this."
"If not, can I ask you something?"
"Oh? What do you want to know?"
His relaxed demeanor while stroking his beard seemed to have lost some of its seriousness.
Is he just happy to be relied upon?
"About the sage's child, Patricia Kindred—her parents, past, friendships, and her proficient magic—everything."
I've been monitoring her movements for the past few days, but all I've gathered is her name.
She's in a different classroom from me and Alicia, and she spends her time there quietly, ignoring the nobles' snide remarks and insults.
After class, she either hangs out with Edward or other target characters, prioritizing Edward somewhat but also diligently deepening her friendships with others.
She also participates in events that take her into town, so it's clear she's a reincarnator like me, aiming for a reverse harem ending.
And everything else about her is truly a mystery.
The Kindred family doesn't exist in my memory, and finding her family in the populous Royal Capital would be a Herculean task.
Unlike Mariana, she's living in the dorms, so I can't follow her.
At this point, my only reliable source is the academy head, Volzeia.
I was prepared for any response, and if he chose to hide something, he might become an enemy depending on the situation.
"That's too much. It's easier for teachers to guide when questions are summarized into one key point."
"I'm not asking a study question, though… What do you want?"
Geez, this is so roundabout.
"If you consider Mariana Ocean to be someone you want to protect, I will give you one truthful answer, based on the pride of Cascade."
Oh, is that all?
She's Alicia's friend and an important character who will be involved in future scenarios, so of course, I want to protect her.
"That's fine. So you'll answer anything, right?"
Anything, huh… like Alicia's measurements?
If I knew that, I'd immediately label her as an enemy right here.
"Hurry up."
Following the impatient old man's command, I felt ridiculous asking about Patricia.
From Mariana's story the other day, I figured she must have been supported by the Ignite family to come to this academy.
Given the situation that seemed like an event in the game, it was clear that Mariana's absence from the academy was deliberately orchestrated.
It would be impossible for the protagonist to mistakenly take the wrong carriage during event timing, and a commoner couldn't swap carriages either.
Considering the information from the magician who came to the Brave Territory, the connection between the Ignite family and Patricia is almost certain.
The Ignite family, which has no daughters, is quite a suspicious clan.
If they show some proof of being able to ensnare Edward, they would likely support her due to a mutual interest.
However, there's one question lingering.
How did a commoner manage to establish a connection with a noble?
The meeting between the protagonist and Edward dates back to their childhood, so any schemes from that time would just be dismissed as childish nonsense.
Could it be that the cunning Ignite family, which has survived by doing various underhanded things, would grant such an absurd level of freedom as a reverse harem?
While they are indeed supporting her, the situation is filled with too many strange points, creating an unsettling atmosphere.
"Nothing? Hurry up."
"Ah, yes, yes."
Pressured, I asked.
"What is the true purpose of the Ignite family?"
"I don't know."
"Hey."
What is this old man, who seems to know everything, saying?
I almost slipped off the roof of the library.
"Isn't what you want to know about Patricia Kindred? I don't know what you're suspicious of, but she was admitted after passing the exam. She didn't enter through any underhanded means."
"Huh."
Whose side is he really on?
"Is that all your questions?"
"Since that wasn't an answer, I still haven't finished asking."
"Very well. Lunch break will end soon. I won't allow you to skip class. Though you sometimes sneak out, don't forget your duty as a student."
"Yes, yes."
Hmm, is he just saying teacher-like things?
It seems like he's only willing to answer based on what he knows within the academy, so I decided to ask something that I thought might interest him.
"Then, why did you support Mariana and help her enroll?"
On top of that, he made me promise to protect her.
If fate is involved, and if this is the eye of the storm of the story, why did he bring her back to the stage?
At my question, Volzeia furrowed his brow for a moment.
Did I hit a sore spot? I'm glad to have gotten a retort!
"It's an enemy territory for commoners, so isn't it contradictory?"
"Well, that is true."
Nodding at my words, Volzeia added, "However,"
"It is the headmaster's duty to allow talented individuals to attend the academy."
"So you're just trying to confuse me."
"Hmm, I suppose I should tell you a bit… Do you believe in fate?"
Fate. It's a word he mentioned when I was told I passed.
"I somewhat believe in it."
In this world, fate means the crappy scenario.
The Brave Territory collapses, and Alicia is possessed by a demon and meets her demise.
It's a terrible product implanted by the production team.
"That would seem to be the case. That's why I'm here."
Please stop with the "that would seem to be the case."
It sounds like he sees through everything, but it's just a joke now.
But it's true that I'm here to prevent that from happening.
"Mariana Ocean has a strong fate."
"That's true."
She's the protagonist who will eventually become the saintess, after all.
"However, that strong fate is now greatly distorted and gone awry."
As I silently listened, Volzeia continued.
"Those with great power are destined to be tossed about by strong fates."
"Nobles of high rank are a good example."
Only royalty and dukes gather around them constantly.
Like moths drawn to light, but they aren't as weak as moths; they are all cunning and try to act in their own interests.
If mishandled, it's a sandcastle that can easily collapse.
"Well, if you stay quiet, you should be fine for now, right?"
In this world, Mariana hasn't done anything particularly noticeable yet.
No, her excessive self-defense to avoid anything happening seems like an effort to stay far from her original fate.
"That's naive. Your will has nothing to do with fate. Lagna Vel Brave, you should know that well."
"That's true."
Imitating his "that would seem to be the case" earned me a glare; my apologies.
Back to the topic, I agree that fate comes crashing in whether you want it or not.
No matter how far you try to distance yourself, it doesn't matter.
To change it, you need to twist it with some other strong power.
"The fate that Mariana Ocean holds will divide the light and darkness of this country."
"How do you know such a thing?"
"That's why I helped her enroll in this academy."
He didn't seem willing to answer why he could say that so confidently.
There is indeed magic that can predict the future.
While it doesn't provide detailed information, it allows glimpses of future scenes.
Volzeia Gran Cascade.
It wouldn't be strange for someone who became a sage after not inheriting the Cascade Duke House and mastering magic to possess such abilities.
He was in a supportive position in the game world as well.
"She has a strong fate, but in this academy, where many others with equally strong fates exist, she will somehow manage, despite the twists and turns."
This otome game depicts the attraction between those with strong fates.
It sounds nice, but for someone destined to perish due to fate, it's unbearable.
"However, right now, Mariana Ocean is outside the intertwining fates at the academy. Alone, without any resistance, she is caught in the great tide of her fate."
Originally, there should have been people like Edward to protect her, but Patricia had taken them all away.
"So, does that mean Patricia has twisted things?"
"I don't know."
Volzeia cut me off sharply and continued.
"Patricia Kindred blatantly distances Mariana from those with strong fates within the academy, and Mariana excessively distances herself as well."
The former protagonist and the current protagonist are like magnets with the same poles.
"I understand the feeling of caution. I don't know where she slipped in from, but it would be better to enroll her than leave her unattended."
"That's true."
If they can manage her, it's better to manage her; I don't know if they can handle it, though.

"Back to the topic. The Brave bloodline also holds a strong fate. A fate so intense that it can twist the fates of others, which is why it has been placed in a lower class. That is why your house is called the stinky monkey of the discarded land."
Wait, hold on, I've never been called a stinky monkey!
I was bewildered by the sudden sharp words in the serious conversation.

"The Brave blood recognizes the struggle against fate as normal, and no matter how harsh the fate may be, it will cling on like a beast until death, until fate runs out. Other nobles unconsciously dislike such blood."
"Huh."
That's quite a heavy burden to bear.
As I listened in silence, the bell signaling the end of lunch rang.
"Class is starting. Let's wrap it up here. Don't be late."
Saying something teacher-like, Volzeia turned on his heel.
"Protect Mariana, who has lost her guardians. If you say this isn't your battlefield, then you should watch her even more closely. Her fate lies not in this box but in a different place."
With that, Volzeia gracefully leaped off the roof of the library.
Parting the moisture in the air, it was as if he were swimming through the sky.
"Alicia, where did we go after leaving my house on our last date?"
"After shopping casually, we bought some skewers from that place you wanted to try."
As I returned my gaze to the bench while seeing off the serious old man, the two were still chatting while preparing to return to class.
"Wait, you had never bought food on the go before? I can understand Alicia, but you too, Lagna?"
"Surprising, right? But he couldn't even ride a train until recently, so he's much more naive about the world than we think."
I was talking about my embarrassing memories from the last date.
The Brave Territory doesn't have trains, and there are no food stalls, so when I actually stopped by, I ended up feeling unexpectedly nervous.
"Is that so!?"
"There's no train in the Brave Territory, so it can't be helped. He's a battle-hardened warrior, but he's completely clueless about ordinary citizens…"
"You seem to understand him well."
He's incredibly strong against combat and rough opponents, but utterly weak against commoners… that's the Brave Family for you.
"I didn't think of him that way, but he's a mysterious guy."
"I thought so at first too, but now I find him quite cute!"
Cute!? Even though he's from the Brave Family, cute!?
"But how nice, going on dates on weekends… Did you hold hands!?"
"Hehe, not only did we hold hands, but I also escorted him!"
"Wha, Alicia did!?"
"Of course!"
Alicia puffed up her chest, leaving Mariana somewhat bewildered.
The story had changed slightly from what she had imagined.
"Since you showed him around the Brave Territory, I'll show him around the Royal Capital."
"Isn't it usually the other way around…?"
"Do you think Lagna could do something like that?"
Alicia cut me off decisively.
"While he might think he has the best date plan in his mind, if he actually tried to execute it, it would probably turn into a disaster. The Royal Capital could very well end up in flames."
"And I want to be equal with him."
Alicia smiled gently and stood up from the bench.
"Come on, don't just stand there; let's hurry back to class! We'll be late!"
"You're right."
As I watched Alicia's back as she started walking, Mariana murmured,
"I can somewhat understand why Lagna is so smitten. She's adorable."
